WHY THIS IS CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS
Three prerequisites already exist: SelectionStore is @Singleton (the selection is app-scoped, so the nav graph can read it), NavGraph already computes canSelectHere, and LocalNavChromeHold landed this week. The prize is not the animation - it is that FOUR screens currently draw their own SelectionBar (Library twice, Search, Browse) and the chrome would draw one.

Morph is the boldest and the cheapest to draw, but it spends something you built on purpose: a pick is meant to survive walking between Browse, Library and Search. With the tabs replaced you cannot reach the other two. 375x62dp also cannot hold a count, four verbs and a way out.

Stack keeps the tabs, so cross-tab picking still works, and there is room for the count line and four verbs. It is today's bar re-homed into the chrome - the smallest behavioural change for the biggest structural win.

The message tier and the verb tier are the same idea at two heights: dock something above the pill, in the pill's own material. That is what makes snackbars and selection stop being two systems. One line only - anything longer, or anything that must not be missed, still belongs in InlineStatus at the top.
